2608.27429.title: Mechanistic Reaction Prediction via Discrete Flow Matching on Graph-Structured Electron Occupation
2608.27429.paper_summary: Chemical reactions are fundamentally transformations in electron space, yet most machine learning approaches model them either through de novo generation of product molecules or through heuristic graph edits that operate directly on molecular topology. We introduce MAELLE (MechAnistic Edit fLow-matching on eLectron rEarrangements), which instead models reactions as discrete flow matching over electron occupation vectors. Concretely, we formulate the reactant-to-product mapping as a Continuous-time Markov Chain (CTMC) over the graph-structured integer-valued electron occupation space defined on all bonding, non-bonding, and hydrogen sites. To construct the interpolants between the reactants and products, we generalize the discrete flow matching mixture path to an edit-based formulation, where the electron moves are interpolated using Optimal Transport, yielding a mechanism-like set of moves without elementary step annotations. MAELLE achieves competitive performance on the USPTO-480K benchmark compared with leading reaction prediction models. Beyond in-distribution learning, we evaluate robustness across two out-of-distribution settings - structural complexity and reaction type - and find that MAELLE maintains strong performance where existing methods degrade. Finally, because the learned flow operates over the full electron redistribution, MAELLE naturally recovers mechanistic trajectories that align with known chemistry and can predict side products of a reaction.
2608.27429.paper_summary_zh: 化學反應基本上是電子空間中的轉變，但大多數機器學習方法要麼通過新生成的產物分子來建模，要麼通過直接作用於分子拓撲的啟發式圖編輯來建模。我們介紹了 MAELLE（機械編輯流匹配電子重排），它將反應建模為電子佔據向量上的離散流匹配。具體而言，我們將反應物到產物的映射公式化為在所有鍵合、非鍵合和氫位點上定義的圖結構整數值電子佔據空間上的連續時間馬爾可夫鏈（CTMC）。為了構建反應物和產物之間的插值，我們將離散流匹配混合路徑推廣到基於編輯的公式，其中電子移動使用最佳運輸進行插值，產生一組類似機制的移動，而不需要基本步驟註解。MAELLE 在與領先的反應預測模型相比的 USPTO-480K 基準測試中達到了競爭力的表現。除了在分佈內學習外，我們還在兩個分佈外的設置中評估了穩健性——結構複雜性和反應類型——發現 MAELLE 在現有方法退化的情況下仍能保持強勁的表現。最後，由於學習的流在整個電子重分配上運作，MAELLE 自然恢復與已知化學相符的機制軌跡，並能預測反應的副產物。
